title: A card's status badge always sits in the same spot
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit (check in Settings > Roles & Permissions > open your role > Work Orders section). The Admin role has both.
  2. Use a desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  3. In the top bar, choose the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Create everything below in this location.
  4. Make sure the location has the technicians this case uses (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff record is Active, Clockable is on, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member > enter the first and last name (e.g. Esther Howard), role Technician, Clockable on, Active, enrolled at this location > Save.
  5. Create the work orders this case uses and set their lead technician (e.g. S1-702 (Approved, long customer name "Fibridge Commercial Transport Services"), S1-455 (Estimate, short name), S1-472 (no unit), all led by Esther Howard):
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose a customer (e.g. "Fibridge Commercial") and an asset (e.g. unit TRK-118, 2022 Freightliner M2) > Create. Write down the number the build gives the work order (the numbers in this case are examples).
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician (e.g. Esther Howard) and save. Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (in the design its tooltip reads "Board").
  4. Look at where the status badge sits on each of the three cards.
  5. Change the density (Density control) to each available option and look again.
  6. Hover each card.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • On every card the status badge is in the same place (in the design: top-right of the card, next to the number), whatever the customer name length or missing unit.
  • It stays in that place at every density and while the card is hovered (the more-actions button appears as an overlay, it does not push the badge aside).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View — board by lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S3-R5, Key Decisions, read 8 Oct 2026. Design: Claude Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Work Orders.dc.html), Board card header; on-screen labels only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R5: “Keep each card’s status badge in a fixed position.”
  • Key Decisions: “More-actions appears as a hover overlay on the card so the status badge sits in a fixed spot instead of floating.”
